## What this notebook checks

Specify the four Light Exposure Behaviour Assessment (LEBA) factor scores and
the full set of exposure metrics before testing them. Report missing data.
Calculate each correlation coefficient and its \(p\)-value using the same
method, then apply one Benjamini--Hochberg correction to the complete
predefined group of tests. The Benjamini--Hochberg procedure limits the
expected proportion of false discoveries among the results treated as
statistically supported.

## What this notebook uses and produces

- Uses: the prepared H05 dataset in `artifacts/06_model_data/H05.rds`.
- Produces: every planned LEBA--exposure comparison, adjusted \(p\)-values,
  effect sizes in interpretable units with 95% confidence intervals, model
  checks, the exact participants, observations, and sites used for each
  comparison, together with missing LEBA factors and exposure outcomes;
  tables, figures, and source data.
- Fixed rule: the H05 metric set is chosen before inspecting H01 results.
- Data sensitivity: fit this identical H05 implementation to the
  manuscript-prepared dataset and compare exact samples, estimates, 95%
  confidence intervals, adjusted results, diagnostics, and conclusions.
